==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|interjeccioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|interjection}} (13th century), from {{der|en|la|interiectiōnem}}, accusative singular of {{m|la|interiectiō||throwing or placing between; interjection}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|intericiō||throw or place between}}, from {{m|la|inter||between}} + {{m|la|iaciō||throw}}. {{surf|en|interject|-ion}}. Displaced {{cog|ang|betwēoxāworpennes|lit=between-thrown-out-ness}}, a [[calque]] of the Latin.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪn.təˈdʒɛk.ʃən/|a=UK}}
* {{enPR|ĭn'tər.jĕkʹshən|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/ˌɪn.tɚˈd͡ʒɛk.ʃən/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-interjection.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|interjection.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛkʃən|s=4}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|grammar}}{{lb|en|countable|grammar}} A [[phrase#Noun|phrase]] or [[word#Noun|word]] with no [[particular#Adjective|particular]] [[grammatical]] [[relation]] to a [[sentence#Noun|sentence]] but which [[serve#Verb|serves]] to [[express#Verb|express]] [[emotion]] or as a [[filled pause]]; an [[exclamation]].
#: {{syn|en|interj<q:abbreviation>|interj.<q:abbreviation>}}
#: {{hypo|en|expletive<id:offensive interjection>}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} Something which is [[interject]]ed; an [[interruption]].
#: {{syn|en|insertion|intercalation|interpolation}}
#* {{RQ:WaPo|date=2020-01-23|author=Philip Bump|title=Mnuchin said Thunberg needed to study economics before offering climate proposals. So we talked to an economist.|text=Mnuchin, asked about climate change in a CNBC interview after his comments about Thunberg, argued there were bigger issues that also needed to be addressed. When a host noted clean air rules as an example of something that might be more urgent, Mnuchin ignored the '''interjection'''.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The act of [[interject]]ing something.
#* {{RQ:WaPo|date=9 February 1986|quotee=w:Carlo Ginzburg|title=Lives: Of Cheese, Witches, No TV And Histories of Common Men|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/opinions/1986/02/09/lives/cc1648fb-6ebd-4873-9078-6b66e6c2acb7/|passage=You can see how those people slowly interjected the inquisitors’ theme about witchcraft, about the witches’ sabbath. And how they slowly transformed their own beliefs into the witchraft beliefs. It took 50 years. I was fascinated by the possibility of reconstructing that kind of '''interjection''' – you interject a self-damaging image, a cultural pattern which is foreign to your own culture, from your enemy, from those judges.}}
#* {{RQ:NYT|date=12 February 2007|author=Cornelia Dean|title=A creationist takes a place in the world of fossils|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260000000000*/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/02/12/health/12iht-create.4568557.html|passage=If researchers like [[w:John Baumgardner|{{quote-gloss|John}} Baumgardner]] do their work “without any form of '''interjection''' of personal dogma,” {{quote-gloss|John}} Geissman said, “I would have to keep as objective a hat on as possible and say, ‘O.K., you earned what you earned.’”}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=16 January 2024|author=w:Marina Hyde|title=If {{w|Harrison Ford}} and {{w|John Travolta}} can be crowned living legends of aviation, why not {{w|Prince Harry}}?|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240116145154/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2024/jan/16/harrison-ford-john-travolta-living-legends-of-aviation-prince-harry|passage=[A]n online petition – perhaps the most ineffectual form of '''interjection''' in modern public life, even including words spoken into the void on [[w:Talk (streaming service)|TalkTV]] – states the decision to honour the Duke of Sussex is a travesty on the part of “such an esteemed organisation”.}}
#* {{RQ:NYT|date=29 April 2026|author=Ben Kenigsberg|title=Three Great Documentaries to Stream|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/29/movies/three-great-documentaries-to-stream.html|passage=The title — sometimes styled with an exclamation point: “[[w:Point of Order (film)|Point of Order!]]” — refers to one of the senator {{quote-gloss|{{w|Joseph McCarthy}}}}’s favored methods of '''interjection'''. He grandstands, he deflects, he insinuates — sometimes to the clear exasperation of his interrogators.}}

More at {{m|en|flow}}. * {{sense|graphite in a pencil}} Graphite was once believed to be a form of lead; see {{m|en|black lead}} and {{m|en|plumbago}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alt|mul|♄||alchemy}} ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/lɛd/|a=RP,GA,CA]}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-lead.wav|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-lead-metal.oga|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Tesco250-lead.wav|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/led/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{rhyme|en|ɛd|s=1}} * {{hmp|en|led}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} [[file:Lead electrolytic and 1cm3 cube.jpg|thumb|Electrolytically refined pure lead]] # {{senseid|en|Q708}} {{lb|en|uncountable}} A heavy, [[pliable]], [[inelastic]] metal [[element]], having a bright, bluish color, but easily [[tarnish]]ed; both [[malleable]] and [[ductile]], though with little [[tenacity]]. It is easily [[fusible]], forms [[alloy]]s with other metals, and is an ingredient of [[solder]] and [[type metal]]. [[atomic number|Atomic number]] 82. #: {{syn|en|mul:Pb|plumbum}} # {{senseid|en|Q1382947}} {{lb|en|countable|nautical}} A [[plummet]] or mass of lead attached to a line, used in [[sound]]ing [[depth]] at sea or to estimate [[velocity]] in [[knots]]. # A thin [[strip]] of [[type metal]], used to [[separate]] lines of type in printing. # {{lb|en|uncountable|typography}} Vertical space in advance of a row or between rows of text. Also known as ''[[leading]]''. #: {{ux|en|This copy has too much '''lead'''; I prefer less space between the lines.}} # [[sheets|Sheet]]s or [[plate]]s of lead [[used]] as a [[covering]] for [[roofs]]. # {{lb|en|countable}} A [[roof]] covered with lead [[sheet]]s or [[terne]] [[plate]]s. #* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|chapter=Of Building|passage=I would have the tower two stories, and goodly '''lead'''s upon the top.}} #* {{RQ:Thackeray Pendennis|passage=These rooms were on a level with the apartments of our friends Bows and Costigan next door at No. 4; and by reaching over the communicating '''leads''', Grady could command the mignonette-box which bloomed in Bows’s window.|43}} # {{senseid|en|Q1936519}} {{lb|en|countable}} A thin [[cylinder]] of [[graphite]] used in [[pencil]]s. #: {{syn|en|pencil lead}} # {{lb|en|slang}} [[bullet|Bullets]]; [[ammunition]]. #: {{ux|en|They [[pump|pumped]] him full of '''lead'''.}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=2012|genre=[[hip-hop]]|artist={{w|Kendrick Lamar|Kendrick Lamar}}|title={{w|Backseat Freestyle|Backseat Freestyle}}|passage=All my life I want money and power

Related to {{cog|ang|līþan|t=to go, travel}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|lede|leed||both|_|obsolete}} ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/ˈliːd/|[ˈlɪi̯d]}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-lead-guide.oga|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|iːd|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|lead}} * {{hmp|en|leed|lede|lied|t3=song}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|led}} # {{senseid|en|guide}}{{lb|en|heading|transitive}} ''To [[guide#Verb|guide]] or [[conduct#Verb|conduct]].'' ## To [[guide]] or [[conduct]] with the hand, or by means of some physical contact connection. ##: {{ux|en|a father '''leads''' a child}} ##: {{ux|en|a jockey '''leads''' a horse with a halter}} ##: {{ux|en|a dog '''leads''' a blind man}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Matthew|15|14|passage=If a blind man '''lead''' a blind man, both fall down in the ditch.}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Luke|4|29|passage=They thrust him out of the city, and '''led''' him unto the brow of the hill.}} ##* {{RQ:Milton Poems|poem=L'Allegro|passage=In thy right hand '''lead''' with thee / The mountain nymph, sweet Liberty.}} ##* {{RQ:Asbjornsen Braekstad Tales|page=271|passage=As he was going home to the palace, he met an old woman '''leading''' a golden goose.}} ## To [[guide]] or conduct in a certain [[course]], or to a certain place or end, by making the way known; to show the way, especially by going with or going in advance of; to [[guide]] somebody somewhere or to [[bring]] somebody somewhere by means of [[instruction]]s. ##: {{ux|en|The guide was able to '''lead''' the tourists through the jungle safely.}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Exodus|13|21|passage=The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to '''lead''' them the way.}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Psalms|23|2|passage=He '''leadeth''' me beside the still waters.}} ##* {{RQ:Milton Poems 1673|sonnet=XXI|passage=This thought might '''lead''' me through the world’s vain mask. Content, though blind, had I no better guide.}} ##* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=I|passage=I stumbled along through the young pines and huckleberry bushes. Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path that, I cal'lated, might '''lead''' to the road I was hunting for. It twisted and turned, and, the first thing I knew, made a sudden bend around a bunch of bayberry scrub and opened out into a big clear space like a lawn.}} ## {{lb|en|figuratively}}: To [[direct]]; to [[counsel]]; to [[instruct]]. ##: {{ux|en|A good teacher should '''lead''' their students to the right answer.}} ## To conduct or [[direct]] with [[authority]]; to have direction or charge of; to [[command]], especially a [[military]] or [[business]] unit. ##: {{syn|en|spearhead}} ##: {{ux|en|to '''lead''' a political party}} ##: {{ux|en|to '''lead''' the search team}} ##* {{RQ:South Sermons|chapter=A Sermon Preached Before the University at Christ-Church, Oxon|year=1664|passage=Christ took not upon him flesh and blood that he might conquer and rule nations, '''lead''' armies, or possess places.}} ## To draw or direct by [[influence]], whether good or bad; to prevail on; to [[induce]]; to entice; to allure. ##: {{ux|en|to '''lead''' someone to a righteous cause}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Matthew|6|13|passage=And '''lead''' us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil|footer=From the [[Lord's Prayer]]. Modernized spelling.}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|2 Timothy|3|6|passage=Silly women, laden with sins, '''led''' away by divers lusts.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1649|author=King {{w|Charles I of England}}|title=w:Eikon Basilike|passage=He was driven by the necessities of the times, more than '''led''' by his own disposition, to any rigor of actions.}} ## To influence towards a belief, a conclusion, etc. ##: {{ux|en|The evidence '''leads''' me to believe he is guilty.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To guide or conduct, as by accompanying, going before, showing, influencing, [[directing]] with authority, etc.; to have [[precedence]] or preeminence; to be first or [[chief]]; — used in most of the senses of the transitive verb. # {{lb|en|heading}} ''To begin, to be ahead.'' ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To go or to be [[in advance]] of; to [[precede]]; hence, to be foremost or chief among. ##: {{syn|en|head|front}} ##: {{ux|en|the big sloop '''led''' the fleet of yachts;  the Guards '''led''' the attack;  Demosthenes '''leads''' the orators of all ages}} ##* '''1600''', {{w|Edward Fairfax}}, The ''{{w|Jerusalem Delivered}}'' of {{w|Torquato Tasso|Tasso}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1819|author=w:Leigh Hunt|title=Abou Ben Adhem |passage=And lo! Ben Adhem's name '''led''' all the rest.}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|passage=“Well,” I answered, at first with uncertainty, then with inspiration, “he would do splendidly to '''lead''' your cotillon, if you think of having one.” ¶ “So you do not dance, Mr. Crocker?” ¶ I was somewhat set back by her perspicuity.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[proceed]] [[in front of]] others; to go first. ##: {{ux|en|The standard-bearers '''led''' and the rest of the marchers followed.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be more advanced in [[technology]] or [[business]] than others. ##: {{ux|en|It '''leads''' in the information technology sector.}} ## {{lb|en|heading|sport}} ### {{lb|en|transitive|cards|dominoes}} To [[begin]] a game, round, or trick, with ###: {{ux|en|to '''lead''' trumps}} ###: {{ux|en|He '''led''' the ace of spades.}} ### {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be [[ahead]] of others, e.g., in a [[race]]. ### {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have the highest interim [[score]] in a [[game]]. ### {{lb|en|baseball}} To step off [[base]] and move towards the next base. ###: {{ux|en|The batter always '''leads''' off base.}} ### {{lb|en|shooting}} To aim in front of a moving [[target]], in order that the [[shot]] may hit the target as it passes. ### {{lb|en|transitive|climbing}} To [[lead climb]]. {{rfclarify|en|"to lead climb" is intransitive(?)}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To tend or reach in a certain spatial [[direction]], or to a certain place. #: {{ux|en|the path '''leads''' to the mill}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Two Gentlemen of Verona|act=V|scene=ii|passage=The mountain-foot that '''leads''' towards Mantua.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be a cause of. {{+obj|en|:to}} #: {{syn|en|lead to}} #: {{ux|en|gambling '''leads''' to other vices}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-10|volume=408|issue=8848|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21583277-worlds-biggest-polluter-going-green-it-needs-speed-up-transition-can-china Can China clean up fast enough?]|passage=All this has '''led''' to an explosion of protest across China, including among a middle class that has discovered nimbyism. That worries the government, which fears that environmental activism could become the foundation for more general political opposition. It is therefore dealing with pollution in two ways—suppression and mitigation.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|usually|with|"[[life]]"}} To live or experience (a particular way of life). #* {{RQ:King James Version|1 Timothy|2|2|text=That we may '''lead''' a quiet and peaceable life.}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|XXXIII|text=Nor thou with shadow'd hint confuse / A life that '''leads''' melodious days.}} #* {{quote-song|en |title=N.I.B. |year=1969 |album=Black Sabbath |artist=Black Sabbath |lyricist=John Osbourne |passage=Follow me now and you will not regret / Leaving the life you '''led''' before we met. / You are the first to have this love of mine, / Forever with me till the end of time.}} # {{used in phrasal verbs|lead off|lead on|lead out|lead to|lead up|lead up to|t4=be the cause of, bring about|lang=en}} # {{misspelling of|en|led}}. =====Conjugation===== {{en-conj|past=led|past_2sg_old2=ledest|old=1}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en |nose-led|one thing led to another|pixie-led|pixy-led|belead |forlead|pixy-lead |forelead |forthlead |inlead |lead astray |lead by the nose |lead captive|leadable|lead to |leader |leading |lead someone down the garden path//lead someone up the garden path |lead the way |lead through |mislead |offlead |onlead|lead around by the nose |outlead|relead| lead someone to the altar |overlead |underlead |all roads lead to Mecca|all roads lead to Rome|all roads lead to Sydney|lead a cat-and-dog life|lead by example|lead from the front|lead nowhere|lead off|lead on|lead out|lead someone a dance|lead the charge|lead the line|lead up|lead up to|lead with one's chin|blind leading the blind|colead|ringlead|uplead}} =====Related terms===== {{col|en|lad|laddie}} =====Translations===== {{see translation subpage|Etymology 2}} ====Noun==== {{wp|+ (news)}} {{en-noun|~}} # {{lb|en|countable}} The act of leading or conducting; ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause or allow (something) to [[remain]] as [[available]]; to [[refrain]] from taking (something) away; to [[stop short]] of consuming or otherwise depleting (something) entirely.
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' my car at home and took a bus to work.}}
##: {{ux|en|The ants did not '''leave''' so much as a crumb of bread.}}
##: {{ux|en|There's not much food '''left'''. We'd better go to the shops.}}
##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=7|passage={{...}} St. Bede's at this period of its history was perhaps the poorest and most miserable parish in the East End of London. Close-packed, crushed by the buttressed height of the railway viaduct, rendered airless by huge walls of factories, it at once banished lively interest from a stranger's mind and '''left''' only a dull oppression of the spirit.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/david-van-tassel David Van Tassel]; [http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/lee-dehaan Lee DeHaan]
|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/wild-plants-to-the-rescue Wild Plants to the Rescue]
|volume=101|issue=3|magazine=w:American Scientist
|passage=Plant breeding is always a numbers game.{{nb...}}. The wild species we use are rich in genetic variation,{{nb...}}. In addition, we are looking for rare alleles, so the more plants we try, the better. These rarities may be new mutations, or they can be existing ones that are neutral—or are even selected against—in a wild population. A good example is mutations that disrupt seed dispersal, '''leaving''' the seeds on the heads long after they are ripe.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive|copulative}} To cause, to result in.
##: {{ux|en|The lightning '''left''' her dazzled for several minutes.}}
##: {{ux|en|Infantile paralysis '''left''' him lame for the rest of his life.}}
##: {{ux|en|She '''left''' disappointed.}}
##: {{ux|en|The accident '''left''' the car a heap of twisted metal.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1899|author=w:Stephen Crane
|title=s:Twelve O'Clock|chapter=1
|passage=There was some laughter, and Roddle was '''left''' free to expand his ideas on the periodic visits of cowboys to the town. “Mason Rickets, he had ten big punkins a-sittin' in front of his store, an' them fellers from the Upside-down-F ranch shot 'em up{{nb...}}.”}}
##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=23|passage=The slightest effort made the patient cough. He would stand leaning on a stick and holding a hand to his side, and when the paroxysm had passed it '''left''' him shaking.}}
##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-20|volume=408| issue=8845| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/http://www.economist.com/news/asia/21582043-villagers-enjoy-sunlight-after-dark-out-gloom Out of the gloom]| passage=[Rural solar plant] schemes are of little help to industry or other heavy users of electricity. Nor is solar power yet as cheap as the grid. For all that, the rapid arrival of electric light to Indian villages is long overdue. When the national grid suffers its next huge outage, as it did in July 2012 when hundreds of millions were '''left''' in the dark, look for specks of light in the villages.}}
## {{senseid|en|deposit (something) and withdraw oneself}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To put; to place; to deposit; to deliver, with a sense of withdrawing oneself.
##: {{ux|en|'''Leave''' your hat in the hall.}}
##: {{ux|en|We should '''leave''' the legal matters to lawyers.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' my sewing and went to the window to watch the falling snow.}}
##* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|5|24|passage='''Leave''' there thy gift before the altar and go thy way.}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|IV|iii|passage=The foot / That '''leaves''' the print of blood where'er it walks.}}
# To depart; to separate from.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[let be]] or do without interference.
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' him to his reflections.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''leave''' my hearers to judge.}}
##: {{ux|en|I'll '''leave''' it to you to decide.}}
## {{senseid|en|depart or depart from}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[depart]] from; to end one's connection or [[affiliation]] with.
##: {{ux|en|His bow and arrow never '''leave'''s him.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' the country and I '''left''' my wife.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=1|passage=I was about to say that I had known the Celebrity from the time he wore kilts. But I see I will have to amend that, because he was not a celebrity then, nor, indeed, did he achieve fame until some time after I '''left''' New York for the West.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[end]] one's [[membership]] in (a group); to terminate one's affiliation with (an organization); to [[stop]] participating in (a project).
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' the band.}}
## {{lb|en|euphemistic|transitive}} To [[die]] (the object denotes those affected by the death).
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To depart; to [[go away]] from a certain place or state.
##: {{syn|en|egress|q1=U.S., formal|absent|exit|make tracks|set forth|Thesaurus:leave}}
##: {{ux|en|I think you'd better '''leave'''.}}
# To transfer something.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[transfer]] [[possession]] of after death.
##: {{ux|en|When my father died, he '''left''' me the house.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[intentionally]] [[place]] (something) to be received by another; to [[deliver]] (something) to a repository; to [[deposit]].
##: {{ux|en|I'll '''leave''' the car in the station so you can pick it up there.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To transfer [[responsibility]] or [[attention]] of (something) (to someone); to [[stop]] being [[concerned]] with.
##: {{ux|en|Can't we just '''leave''' this to the experts?}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[remain]] (behind); to [[stay]].
